在生活還沒被迫劇烈改變之前，: before life is forced to change drastically,
後設認知，就是知道自己正在怎麼想。: Metacognition means knowing how you are thinking.
平常我們想事情，通常會直接跟著自己的想法走。後設認知多了一步：退後半步，看看自己: Usually, when we think about something, we just follow our thoughts wherever they go. Metacognition adds one step: take half a step back and notice which way of thinking you are using right now to make sense of what is in front of you.
開會的時候，被同事一句話惹到，正準備回嘴。: You are in a meeting. A colleague says something that gets under your skin, and you are about to snap back.
這時候，如果心裡突然冒出一句：「我現在很想贏。」: Right then, a thought pops up: "Right now I really want to win."
事情沒有變，同事也沒有變。但我們多了一個選擇：繼續照原本的反應走，或是換一種方式: Nothing about the situation has changed, and neither has your colleague. But now you have a choice: carry on with your usual reaction, or respond in a different way.
為什麼還要「固定留白」: Why we also need "regular blank space"
看得見自己的想法，和有時間去調整，是兩件事。: Seeing your own thoughts and having time to adjust them are two different things.
很多人其實看得見，只是每天忙著趕事情，沒有一段安靜的時間，好好想想自己剛才看見了: Many people can see their thoughts just fine. They are simply rushing through every day, with no quiet stretch of time to think over what they just noticed.
有時候，一場大事件會讓人被迫停下來，重新思考原本習慣的生活方式。: Sometimes a major event forces a person to stop and rethink the way of living they were used to.
固定留白，就是我們自己先把這段時間空出來，不用等到事情發生，才開始回頭看。: Regular blank space means we clear that time ourselves first, so we do not have to wait for something to happen before we start looking back.
和治理層的關係: How it relates to the steering layer
在我們的世界觀裡，治理層講的是：所有聲音都聽，方向盤在現在的你手上。: In our worldview, the steering layer means this: listen to every voice, with the steering wheel in the hands of the you of this moment.
但要聽見這些聲音，我們得先學會退後半步，看看自己正在想什麼、感受什麼。: To hear all those voices, though, we first need to learn to step back half a step and notice what we are thinking and feeling.
所以，後設認知就像進門的第一步。: So metacognition is like the first step through the door.
進門以後，我們還是要自己做決定，也要為自己的選擇負責。: Once we are inside, we still make our own decisions and take responsibility for our own choices.

研究說了什麼，沒說什麼: What the research says, and what it doesn't
研究參考｜後設認知與大腦的研究: Research reference | Studies on metacognition and the brain
英國教育基金會（EEF）整理了 355 篇研究，發現後設認知的方法可以透過教學來: The Education Endowment Foundation (EEF) in the UK reviewed 355 studies and found that metacognitive methods can be learned through teaching. Students who used these methods made, on average, 8 extra months of learning progress in a year (updated May 2025).
另一份 2018 年的統合分析，整理了 48 個教學研究。結果發現，教完當下有效: Another meta-analysis, from 2018, pooled 48 teaching studies. It found that the teaching helped right away, and the effect was still there when students were tested again after some time (effect size 0.50, and 0.63 at follow-up).
那麼，長期練習會不會讓大腦跟著改變？: So can long-term practice change the brain as well?
2011 年有一份研究，追蹤了受訓四年的倫敦計程車司機。研究發現，成功考上執照的: A 2011 study followed London taxi drivers through four years of training. It found that among the drivers who passed the licensing exam, gray matter increased in the posterior hippocampus, the part of the brain that handles spatial memory. The drivers who did not pass, and the control group, did not show this change.
不過，這裡有兩件事要說清楚。: That said, there are two things we want to be clear about.
第一，上面這些研究，觀察的是學生的學習，以及認路這類技能。我們不能直接拿這些結果: First, the studies above looked at students' learning and at skills such as finding your way around. We cannot use these results to conclude that every self-awareness practice would have the same effect.
第二，覺察練習到底會不會改變大腦結構，目前的研究結果還不一致。2011 年一份小: Second, whether awareness practice changes brain structure is still unsettled. A small 2011 study (16 people versus 17 people) observed changes, but a 2022 randomized study with 218 participants did not see the same result.
至於我們提到的「提前醒來」，以及「後設認知是治理層的前提」，目前也還沒有研究直接: As for the idea of "waking up ahead of time" that we mentioned, and the idea that "metacognition is the precondition for the steering layer," no study has directly tested either one yet.
Education Endowment Foundation, Teaching: Education Endowment Foundation, Teaching and Learning Toolkit: Metacognition and self-regulation (updated May 2025)
當我們能看見自己正在怎麼想，就比較有機會自己做選擇，少一點照著習慣或別人的話走。: When we can see how we are thinking, we have a better chance of making our own choices, and we follow habit or other people's words a little less. This is what we call "rewriting the script."
研究參考｜看得懂自己，和幸福感: Research reference | Understanding yourself, and well-being
有研究把「常常想自己」和「看得懂自己」分開來看，發現和生活滿意度、心理幸福感有關: Some research separated "thinking about yourself often" from "understanding yourself," and found that the part linked to life satisfaction and psychological well-being was "understanding yourself" (121 university students, 2011). Another study of 227 people (2014) found something similar: simply reflecting often is not necessarily better, and whether you can see yourself clearly is the part linked to well-being.
至於「比較不容易被別人的意見左右」，目前的研究結果並不一致，有些小型實驗甚至出現: As for "being less easily swayed by other people's opinions," the research results so far are mixed, and some small experiments even found the opposite. So we keep this part as Molly's own experience and share it as it is.
練熟了之後，還有這些好處: After you have practiced for a while, there are more benefits
下面每一點，我們都有標出它屬於「有研究」還是「個人感受」。其中，個人感受來自 M: For every point below, we have marked whether it is "backed by research" or "personal experience." The personal experience comes from what Molly has built up over many years of practice, and no research has directly tested it yet.
一、看得到根源，就比較不會一直重來: 1. When you can see the root, you are less likely to keep starting over
「這個能力變得很習慣的時候，你比較容易拆解事情的本質，而不會一直在重蹈覆轍。」: "Once this ability has become a habit, it is easier to break down the essence of things, and you do not keep repeating the same mistakes."
「你會更了解自己，為什麼現在在拖延？為什麼現在在恐懼？」: "You understand yourself better: why am I procrastinating right now? Why am I afraid right now?"
當同樣的事情一再發生時，可以試著多問自己一句「我為什麼又這樣」，就比較有機會找到: When the same thing keeps happening, you can try asking yourself one more question, "Why am I doing this again?" and you have a better chance of finding the reason behind it.
二、處理根源，不只處理表面: 2. Working on the root, beyond the surface
「大部分的人如果沒有練習這件事情，大家處理的通常都是表象。」: "If most people have not practiced this, what they deal with is usually just the surface."
「有些人就會去選擇去逃避、去喝酒、去麻痺自己，或是想說就是裝作不知道。可是其實問: "Some people choose to escape, to drink, to numb themselves, or they just pretend they do not know. But the problem has never actually been solved, so it keeps happening."
有研究（講的是「逃避」這一半）。: Backed by research (this covers the "avoidance" half).
研究參考｜逃避，和之後的壓力事件: Research reference | Avoidance, and later stressful events
有一份研究追蹤了 1,211 人，時間長達十年。研究發現，一開始越習慣用逃避的方: One study followed 1,211 people for ten years. It found that the more a person habitually dealt with stress by avoiding it at the start, the more stressful events that person ran into four years later.
這裡要說清楚：這份研究的對象是五、六十歲的人，測量的是「習慣逃避」，並沒有測量後: One thing to make clear: this study looked at people in their fifties and sixties, and it measured "a habit of avoidance," not metacognition. As for "people who can see the essence are better at solving it," that is Molly's own experience.
三、比較不容易被話術帶走: 3. Less easily carried away by manipulative talk
「很多人都說想要做自己，可是其實常常還是會不自覺的在過別人認為好的人生。」: "Many people say they want to be themselves, but in fact they often end up, without realizing it, living the life other people think is good."
「你有練習這個能力的好處是，你可以破解很多的話術。」: "The benefit of practicing this ability is that you can see through a lot of manipulative talk."
研究參考｜事先認識話術: Research reference | Learning about manipulation tactics in advance
2022 年有一組研究做了七個實驗，先讓參與者認識一些常見的操弄手法，像是使用情: A set of studies in 2022 ran seven experiments. Participants first learned about some common manipulation techniques, such as using emotional language, offering only two options, or blaming a scapegoat.
其中，六個隨機分組實驗共有 6,464 人，另外還有一項在 YouTube 上進: Six of them were randomized experiments with 6,464 people in total, and there was also a field test on YouTube with 22,632 participants. The results showed that people who had learned about these techniques beforehand found it easier to recognize them, and were better at telling which content was trustworthy.
不過，這些研究練習的是「認識別人的手法」，和「看懂自己」還是有些不同，所以我們把: That said, what these studies trained was "recognizing other people's techniques," which is somewhat different from "understanding yourself," so we have marked it as indirectly related. As for "unconsciously living the life others think is good," that is Molly's own experience.
四、越會讀自己，也越會讀別人: 4. The better you read yourself, the better you read others
「你只要越來越熟練怎麼讀懂自己，你就越來越能夠讀懂別人，所以我覺得同理心會更高吧: "The more skilled you become at reading yourself, the better you can read others, so I think your empathy will be higher."
前半句有研究，後半句是個人感受。: The first half is backed by research, and the second half is personal experience.
研究參考｜認識自己裡面不同的部分: Research reference | Getting to know the different parts inside yourself
2017 年有一份研究，找了兩組人（80 人和 81 人），花三個月練習辨認「自: A 2017 study had two groups of people (80 and 81 people) spend three months practicing how to recognize "the different parts inside themselves."
結果發現，能辨認出越多部分的人，在理解別人想法和意圖的能力上，進步也越多。: It found that the more parts a person could recognize, the more that person improved at understanding what other people think and intend.
這份研究測量的是「理解別人在想什麼」，沒有測量同理心。所以「同理心會更高」這一部: This study measured "understanding what others are thinking," and it did not measure empathy. So for the part about "empathy will be higher," we have marked it as personal experience.
「很多事情你一旦看到的是本質，你就有辦法越過很多的情緒，而不會被表象給絆住。」: "With many things, once you see the essence, you are able to get past a lot of emotions and not get tripped up by the surface."
我們的理解是：當我們慢慢看懂事情背後的原因，就比較不容易被情緒牽著走。當然，情緒: Our understanding is this: as we slowly come to see the reasons behind things, we are less easily led around by our emotions. Of course, emotions are also worth listening to, because they carry messages themselves.
五、越認識自己，越能自在獨處: 5. The better you know yourself, the more at ease you are alone
「我覺得人性就是對於未知的東西會很恐懼。」: "I think it is human nature to be very afraid of the unknown."
「如果你練習得很熟練的話，你會比較不害怕與自己獨處。我覺得很多人會很害怕孤單或是: "If you practice until you are very skilled, you will be less afraid of being alone with yourself. I think many people are very afraid of being lonely, and that comes from this fear of the unknown. When you do not know yourself well enough, you do not know how to face yourself when you are alone, and you want to reach outward. But when you know yourself well enough, you actually find out that you are a book with a lot in it to read."
一個人的時候覺得空空的，有時候是因為還不太了解自己。隨著慢慢認識自己，也會越來越: Feeling empty when you are alone is sometimes because you do not yet know yourself very well. As you slowly get to know yourself, you also come to know more and more how to keep yourself company when you are alone.
六、越能接納自己，也越懂得尊重別人: 6. The more you accept yourself, the better you respect others
「還有就是你會比較能夠接納自己，因為你都看得見原因，你就不會隨便的批評自己。所以: "And another thing is that you will be better able to accept yourself. Because you can see the reasons, you will not criticize yourself carelessly. So in the same way, you will also be less likely to criticize others, because you can see some of the reasons, and only then can you truly show respect."
當我們慢慢看懂自己為什麼會這樣，就比較不會急著責怪自己。看待別人的時候，也能多一: As we slowly understand why we are the way we are, we are less quick to blame ourselves. When we look at other people, we can also be a bit more understanding.
一邊過日子，一邊觀察自己怎麼過日子，就像同時開了兩個視角。看見的東西變多了，也會: Living your days while also watching how you live them is like opening two viewpoints at once. You see more, and it also takes more energy.
研究參考｜把注意力放在自己身上: Research reference | Putting your attention on yourself
一、注意力放在自己身上，其實有兩種不同的方式。1999 年的研究把它分成「反思」: First, there are actually two different ways to put your attention on yourself. A 1999 study divided them into "reflection" and "rumination": reflection means observing yourself with curiosity, and rumination means going over the same thing again and again without being able to stop. A person can come to understand herself better and, at the same time, feel worse. The researchers called this the "paradox of self-absorption."
二、2002 年一份整合 226 個效果量的統合分析發現，整體來看，越常把注意力: Second, a 2002 meta-analysis that combined 226 effect sizes found that, overall, the more often people put their attention on themselves, the more negative emotion they had. Within that, the link between rumination and negative emotion was stronger than the link for self-focus in general.
三、2010 年刊在《Science》的一份研究，透過手機隨機詢問人們「你現在在: Third, a study published in Science in 2010 used phones to ask people at random "What are you thinking about right now?" and found that we often think about things other than what is happening in front of us, and that these are usually also the times we are less happy.
四、2001 年的高爾夫推桿實驗發現，對已經很熟練的動作，如果在壓力下還一步一步: Fourth, a 2001 golf-putting experiment found that for a movement someone has already mastered, watching yourself step by step under pressure can make performance worse.
所以留白要包含「真的放空」: So blank space has to include "really zoning out"
留白可以有兩種方式。一種是坐下來，回頭看看自己，這是練習。另一種是暫時放下觀察和: Blank space can take two forms. One is sitting down and looking back at yourself, and that is practice. The other is setting aside observation and analysis for a while so you can really rest. Both are worth making room for in your life.
研究參考｜休息不等於閒著: Research reference | Rest is not idleness
2012 年有一篇回顧，整理了大腦在休息時的運作，標題就叫〈休息不等於閒著〉。人: A 2012 review summarized how the brain works at rest, and its title is "Rest Is Not Idleness." When people zone out, the brain still handles memory, imagines the future, and sorts out feelings about relationships. The authors believe we need to find a balance between focusing outward and resting inward.
要說清楚的是，上面這些研究大多來自問卷和實驗室作業，觀察的是一般人的自我關注、反: One thing to make clear: most of the studies above come from questionnaires and lab tasks, and they looked at self-focus, rumination and rest in ordinary people. They did not directly study "people who have practiced metacognition until they are very good at it." The benefits and costs of practice come from Molly's own first-hand observation of herself over a year or more of practice.
每天留幾分鐘，回頭看看自己今天的情緒、精力，還有做過的事。: Each day, set aside a few minutes to look back at how you felt today, how much energy you had, and what you did.

從看見、到改變行為、改寫神經迴路的整個過程，: The whole process, from seeing, to changing behavior, to rewriting neural circuits,

「這個能力你練得越熟悉，你越能夠把主導權放回自己身上，你也越不容易被別人的意見左: "The more familiar you become with this ability, the more you can put the lead back in your own hands, and the less easily you are swayed by other people's opinions"
